title: DerivedCohomologyGermIso
statement: For every scheme S, geometric point s, L in D⁺(Ab(S_et)) and integer n, the canonical comparison from derived sections to sections of H^n(L) [def-weil-pbc-canonical-derived-cohomology-germs] induces an isomorphism on geometric stalks. This is the sheafification comparison and has no strict-local continuity or mate assertion.

source.place: Tags 03Q9, 03Q8 and 0BKV; neighbourhood colimit and final injective-complex paragraph

proof.text:
represent L[n] by a bounded below K-injective complex M. The derived Hom from
Z[U][0] is represented by cycles in M(U), modulo boundaries. The displayed map sends
such a cycle to its homology section. Locally, every homology section lifts to a cycle,
because cycles surject onto the homology sheaf. If the homology section of a cycle
vanishes, locally the cycle lifts through the differential from degree -1; the lift is
a null homotopy of the map from Z[U][0]. Hence the comparison is locally bijective.
Sheafification makes it an isomorphism, and geometric stalks are unchanged by
sheafification. Finally the homology shift isomorphism transports H^0(L[n]) to H^n(L).
The cycle and boundary argument applies for every integer n and also for L = 0.

mathlib_searches.results: Eight results about structure-sheaf stalks and ordinary module pullback; none realizes these abelian derived-section maps. Loogle presheafToSheaf, homology and IsPullback, IsAffineHom queries returned no hits.

Mathlib has general stalk and pullback infrastructure, but no strict-local derived mate or the canonical derived Hom-to-germ comparison. The existing AbelianHigherDirectImagePresheaf has private definitions of the comparison, inaccessible from another module.
